newsitem.title: USA: Freeport sees rising commodity prices.
newsitem.headline: Freeport sees rising commodity prices.

text.p: Freeport-McMoRan Resources Partners said Tuesday that expectations for higher corn and soybean acreage this spring, coupled with rising commodity prices, bode well for increased domestic phosphate fertilizer sales in the second quarter.

The company said Diammonium phosphate (DAP) unit production costs at IMC-Agrico's plants declined about five percent from the year-ago quarter as a result of reduced phosphate rock, sulphur and processing costs.
The company said unit costs for the near term will benefit from the decline in ammonia prices which occurred during the first quarter of 1997.
The company said ammonia prices show indications of further weakness in the Gulf Coast region.
The company said the long-term outlook for the phosphate fertilizer industry remains very positive.

Increasing world population and improving diets in developing countries, combined with historically low grain stocks, necessitate greater agricultural output, which will require higher fertilizer use, the company said.
Strong demand growth projected in Asia and Latin America is expected to require additional supplies beyond the global industry's current production capability, the company said.
